patch.value: Evaluate proposer transfer on a statistically powered tracker corpus

The bounded recursive-improver acceptance uses two independent meta trackers, below the unchanged ten-sample outer gate minimum. Plan a larger independent public tracker/task benchmark with an explicit power analysis, preserve chronological and meta/audit separation, and repeat equal-budget proposer comparisons without relaxing the promotion gate.

The bounded recursive-improver acceptance uses two distinct meta trackers, below the unchanged ten-sample outer gate minimum; item-level inner bounds are also underpowered on the small chronological cohorts. Plan a larger public tracker/task benchmark with an explicit power analysis, account for correlated fleet work, preserve chronological and meta/audit separation, and repeat equal-budget proposer comparisons without relaxing the promotion gate.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Plan: freeze public commit-pinned tracker-disjoint development/meta/audit sources; declare a 0.10 transfer effect, 0.01 promotion margin, alpha 0.05 and target power 0.80 before measuring. Use bounded paired tracker means with task and generation Bonferroni correction. Preserve existing promotion gates and refuse underpowered evidence. Seal replayable corpus/split/evaluation context in SDK-owned items and native history; run one CPU-niced bounded real generation, report all refusals honestly.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Corpus frozen before scoring: 31 public MIT source pins, 19 development tasks, 16 meta tasks and 11 audit tasks; corpus digest 7156cf8c85b9941e12e42632c08f27419af69b7b3ee8824545c35def3fee9d49. One unverifiable directory excluded; private/hosted sources never opened. Conservative declared power requires 3062 held-out trackers per task; the available fleet cannot meet this. Proceeding with one bounded diagnostic generation, not claiming powered no-transfer evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Runtime adjustment before a complete held-out comparison: stopped the broad diagnostic after 19 development fits and one meta-baseline fit, preserving receipts, reservations and any cancellation transition. A second predeclared diagnostic selects the first three trackers with both tasks in each compartment by SHA-256 repository identity and seed 42, with no score-based selection. One generation, one proposal, 64 updates, 10-minute deadline in an isolated non-git SDK tracker. Native corpus, paired observations and replayable decisions are copied through SDK APIs into this tracker; no evidence side files are published.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Behavioral revert proofs in a disposable copy: removing only requireProposerTransfer made the underpowered native SDK test fail (exit 1); removing only verifyTransferCorpus made both training/held-out leakage and native split-digest replay tests fail (exit 1). All failures were assertion failures, not import/build failures; each function was restored in finally. Focused corpus/privacy/native replay tests pass 6/6.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Real diagnostic completed: 1 generation, 30 fits, 1920 optimizer updates, 5 proposal processes, zero inference tokens, 576.235 seconds including verified native publication. Meta trackers: pm-context, pm-ops, pm-graph. Audit: pm-linear, pm-vcs, pm-starter. Both targets had accuracy 0.50 versus 0.50, paired effect 0.00, simultaneous interval [-1.00,1.00], n=3 and prospective power lower bound 0.00; 3062 trackers per task required. Decision transfer_underpowered, zero promotions, original proposer retained. The audit consequently compares the retained original with itself. No claim of powered no-transfer or improvement. Native result rsipower-bounded-result and digest-addressed corpus/evaluation Decisions retain replayable context. SDK gaps: none encountered; linked tests pass using pm-context none with workspace snapshot (3/3); automatic linked-result storage is disabled by existing project configuration, so this comment retains the result.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Issue 149 confirmed by exact byte bound: the prior single native root cannot hold the minimum powered reference list. Replacing new archives with content-addressed ordered shards covering both source metadata and tasks, plus a small root; retain version-one receipt replay. New executions will seal explicit operator effect/alpha/power and generation-derived look count in a native plan before scoring. Regression will archive/replay the actual 3062-tracker-per-task minimum through a real non-git SDK tracker, retain every record cap, and exercise missing/extra/reordered/tampered shards.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Issue 149 targeted native regression passed 4/4. The original minimum (3062 trackers per task, 12248 meta/audit tasks plus development) archives and replays successfully in a real non-git SDK tracker: 73 shards, 5412-byte root, maximum record 264191 bytes, all below the unchanged 1048576-byte limit. Its synthetic favorable paired comparison also passes the explicit transfer plan and replays. Missing, extra, duplicated, reordered and altered shards refuse; oversize entries refuse before native writes. Prospective effect/alpha/power and generation-derived looks are now native plan context, with legacy version-one replay retained.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Behavioral reverts passed 6/6 in disposable copies with every mutation restored in finally. In addition to the original three guards, reverting only archiveTransferCorpus to the pre-fix implementation fails the minimum-powered native archive test with json_record_limit; removing only shard-position validation fails missing/extra/reorder regression with a missing-rejection assertion; restoring fixed power choices inside transferPower fails the explicit-design regression. No missing import or syntax error was accepted as proof. Native source/task shards keep each record bounded and legacy roots remain readable.
